podcast.body: First heard in June 1995 while driving on the 101 Freeway in Los Angeles, this song was immediately recognized for its intense anger and was likened to "revenge porn set to music." It marked a profound transformation for Alanis Morissette from a "wannabe pop starlet" to a formidable alt-rock figure, with a real breakup experience providing its emotional core. "It was June of 1995. I was listening to the radio, driving up the 101 Freeway in Los Angeles. Wow, said my wife, who was in the car with me. That is an angry song. I love it."

podcast.body: From the album "Jagged Little Pill," this song led to extensive public speculation regarding the identity of the ex-boyfriend it addresses. Various individuals were suggested as the subject, including Mike Paluso (New Jersey Devils, Ottawa Senators), Doug Gilmore (Toronto Maple Leafs), Matt Leblanc (Friends, appeared in an Alanis video), Bob Saget, Leslie Howe (a member of Alanis' backup band for her first two albums), and Ryan Reynolds, though Reynolds was disqualified because he dated Alanis between 2002 and 2004, years after the song's release. The most widely believed subject is Dave Coulier, an American stand-up comic and actor (Joey Gladstone in Full House), who dated Alanis in the early 1990s and broke up with her in 1994, just as she began working on material for "Jagged Little Pill." Coulier himself has stated that certain elements in the song "really sounded familiar." Alanis has maintained that she never reveals the subjects of her songs, writing them for personal expression rather than for others. "It appears that the ex-boyfriend in question is Dave Cullier, an American stand-up comic and the guy who played Joey Gladstone in the sitcom Full House."

podcast.body: This song became Alanis Morissette's breakthrough hit in 1995, described as a diss record that "deployed one very catchy F-bomb." It is widely rumored to be an "evisceration of her former boyfriend, Full House TV star Dave Coulier," a claim Morissette has since denied, though Coulier believes it's about him. "You ought to know, is rumored to be Alanis Morissette's evisceration of her former boyfriend, Full House TV star Dave Coulier."

podcast.body: This song, the first single from *Jagged Little Pill*, was released in the summer of 1995. It started on alternative radio and quickly became a generational anthem, articulating the feelings many people had about certain relationships. Speculation surrounded the identity of the song's subject, with names like comedian Dave Coulier, Mike Peluso of the New Jersey Devils, Matt LeBlanc from *Friends*, or Canadian producer Leslie Howe (who produced her first two albums) being suggested. "You want to know, started out on alternative radio and then spread and spread and spread until it became this generational anthem."
